title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 47
paragraphs: Accompanying Dorieus and dying with him was also Philip, son of Butacides, a man of Croton, who, having been betrothed to the daughter of Telys the Sybarite, had become an exile from Croton; then, disappointed of the marriage, he sailed off to Cyrene, and from there set out and accompanied Dorieus with a trireme of his own, supplying the expenses of the crew himself. This man had been a victor at the Olympic games and was the most beautiful of the Hellenes of his time; and because of his beauty he received from the men of Egesta what no one else ever received from them—they established a hero-shrine over his tomb and still propitiate him with sacrifices.
